title: Observation of correlations beyond the single-particle picture in fermionic counting statistics
authors: Johann Zöllner, Hendrik Mannel, Daniel Oppers, Martin Geller, Axel Lorke, Jürgen König
abstract: The analysis of charge fluctuations in a mesoscopic device can shed light on the fundamental question of whether or not a single-particle picture of electron transport is appropriate, even in the presence of Coulomb interaction. It has been shown on general grounds that mapping the interacting system onto a fermionic single-particle description is subject to strict constraints on the charge-transfer statistics. These constraints can be formulated in terms of a sign rule for the factorial cumulants of the full counting statistics. We report here on the experimental observation of a sign-rule violation in a most elementary model system, i.e. a single-level quantum dot, and provide theoretical modeling that can quantitatively reproduce the experimental data. This reveals the presence of correlations introduced by electron-electron interaction.
summary: This paper experimentally demonstrates that charge fluctuations in a quantum dot violate a theoretical sign rule derived for non-interacting fermions. By analyzing the full counting statistics, the authors provide quantitative evidence that electron-electron interactions introduce correlations beyond the single-particle picture in mesoscopic transport.
main_problem: The study aims to determine if electron transport in mesoscopic devices, even when Coulomb interactions are present, can still be accurately described by a simple single-particle picture.
main_result: The authors report the first experimental observation of a violation of a specific sign rule in fermionic counting statistics within a single-level quantum dot, providing evidence for electron-electron correlations.
method: The analysis relies on measuring and analyzing the factorial cumulants of the charge-transfer statistics, comparing them against theoretical constraints derived from single-particle models.
model_or_system: The system is a single-level quantum dot tunnel-coupled to reservoirs, controlled by gate voltage and subjected to a tuneable magnetic field. The theoretical modeling uses a state-and-N-resolved master equation.
key_observables: Factorial cumulants of the full counting statistics (e.g., second-, third-, and fourth-order cumulants) extracted from photon counting measurements.
important_parameters: The magnetic field ($B$) is the key parameter controlling the appearance of the sign-rule violation; the system is analyzed in regimes where spin degeneracy is lifted.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the charge-transfer statistics can be fully characterized by the factorial cumulants, and that the charging energy is large enough to prevent double occupancy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup (quantum dot structure) and the measurement signal, which is a random telegraph signal derived from monitoring resonance fluorescence during electron ejection events.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical criterion (sign rule violation) for interaction effects, details the experimental realization in a quantum dot, and presents the quantitative measurement and theoretical modeling that confirms the violation.
why_interesting: This work directly probes the breakdown of single-particle descriptions in interacting quantum systems, which is a central theme in strongly correlated electron physics and open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) The sample consists of a gate layer, the quantum- dot layer containing the investigated quantum dot, and a reservoir layer. The states of the quantum dot can be ma- nipulated by gate voltage VG and magnetic field B. Electrons tunnel into the quantum dot (black arrow) and leave it via Auger processes caused by the trion laser (red). The occu- pation of the quantum dot is tracked using resonance fluo- rescence induced by the exciton laser (green). (b) Telegraph signal resulting from detected photons, which indicates the occupation of the quantum dot. The number of photons de- tected within the interval tbin = 60 µs is tracked over time.

FIG. 2. (a) Relevant states and possible transitions between them. (b) Particles involved for each state with electrons represented by filled circles and holes represented by empty circles. The confining potential is sketched as a rectangular quantum well for the electron and as an inverted quantum well for the hole. (c) Simplified three-state model. Exciton state |X0⟩and unoccupied state |0⟩as well as trion state |X↑⟩and spin-up state |↑⟩have been combined. (d) Two-state model, applicable for very small or very large magnetic fields.

FIG. 3. Factorial cumulants as a function of the time interval for magnetic fields (a) B = 0 T, (b) B = 0.5 T, (c) B = 2 T, (d) B = 3.25 T, (e) B = 6 T, and (f) B = 10 T. The experimental data is shown as dots, the model calculations as straight lines and the expected standard deviation from the model as colored regions. In (b)-(d), some of the factorial cumulants change sign, while following the sign rule (6) in (a) and (f).
